title: [Parinaud syndrome : a diplopia unlike any other].

We report three patients in whom a traumatic thoracolumbar burst fracture produced features of CMS and describe their operative management. A 57-year-old man with an L1 burst fracture and intact leg power presented with bowel and bladder incontinence and underwent posterior stabilization (D11-L3), regaining continence early. title: C5-Predominant Segmental Zoster Paresis Presenting With Right Shoulder Abduction Weakness Before Cutaneous Eruption: A Case Report.
summary: Segmental zoster paresis (SZP) is an uncommon motor complication of herpes zoster (HZ) characterized by focal, asymmetric weakness in a myotomal distribution. Motor weakness usually follows the cutaneous eruption, and pre-eruptive weakness can mimic cervical radiculopathy, brachial plexopathy, neuralgic amyotrophy, or other causes of acute focal limb weakness. A 57-year-old woman developed right shoulder pain and, five days later, became unable to abduct her right arm. A vesicular eruption appeared on the lateral aspect of the right upper arm three days after the onset of weakness, and HZ was diagnosed. title: An unusual presentation of chronic granulomatous invasive fungal rhinosinusitis: A case report and review of the literature.
summary: Granulomatous chronic invasive fungal rhinosinusitis (GCIFR) is an atypical form of invasive fungal rhinosinusitis which affects immunocompetent middle-aged adults mainly due to Aspergillus flavus. It presents with symptoms like headache, facial pain, and proptosis, primarily affecting the ethmoid and maxillary sinuses, and can lead to serious complications. This report details a unique case of GCIFR treated with antifungal and corticosteroid therapy. A 27-year-old Persian male was admitted with left exophthalmia, diplopia, facial pain, and paresthesia. title: Cardiac Metastasis From Lung Cancer: A Hidden Cardioembolic Source of Acute Ischemic Stroke.
summary: Acute ischemic stroke requires prompt identification of the underlying mechanism to guide treatment and secondary prevention. Although common causes account for most cases, occasionally the diagnostic work-up reveals an unexpected cardioembolic source. We report the case of a woman in her 50s with stage IVB non-small cell lung carcinoma who was admitted with presyncope, acute disorientation, and dysarthria, followed by anomia and right-sided neurological deficits. title: Passive intraoperative motor fMRI under general anesthesia during open-craniotomy glioma surgery: a prospective technical feasibility study.
summary: Sensorimotor localization is important during peri-Rolandic glioma surgery. We assessed passive intraoperative motor functional MRI (pifMRI) under general anesthesia. Can pifMRI provide useable sensorimotor maps before and after resection for neuronavigation and comparison with cortical stimulation? Eight adults (24-72 years; median, 57.5) underwent pifMRI intraoperatively in a two-room 3-T intraoperative MRI setting. With cranium open, blood oxygen level-dependent signals were elicited by passive flexion-extension of digits II-V. title: Contrastive adversarial mix-up learning for unsupervised cross-modality image segmentation.
summary: Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) has been extensively investigated in terms of its ability to address the performance degradation caused by distribution shifts between labeled source-domain images and unlabeled target-domain images. In radiotherapy, this problem is particularly relevant for the transfer of segmentation knowledge from planning computed tomography (CT) to cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), for which target-domain annotations are limited. This study aimed to develop a contrastive adversarial mix-up learning framework for unsupervised cross-modality image segmentation. title: Vessel wall MRI predictors of postprocedural new ischemic brain lesions after endovascular treatment for basilar artery stenosis.
summary: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)-detected new ischemic brain lesions (NIBL) are common complications after endovascular treatment (EVT) for basilar artery stenosis (BAS), directly impacting functional outcomes in patients. This study aimed to explore the association between vulnerable plaque markers identified by high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (HR-MRI) and NIBL, and to clarify their predictive value for postprocedural ischemic events. A total of 373 patients with BAS who underwent EVT were retrospectively enrolled in this study. Patients were classified into DWI-positive (DWI+) and DWI-negative (DWI-) groups based on the presence of NIBL on DWI within 48 hours post-procedurally.

title: Neural correlates and sex hormonal associations of impaired feedback-learning in adolescent patients with anorexia nervosa - a longitudinal fMRI study.
summary: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a somato-psychiatric disease that mostly begins in adolescence, involving endocrine changes including amenorrhea. It is difficult to treat as most patients have difficulties embracing change and thus, the disease often takes a chronic course. Underlying pathomechanisms including moderate neuropsychological deficits of learning and memory remain insufficiently understood. title: From localized to long-range: functional connectivity alterations in mild to moderate chronic low back pain patients.
summary: Mild pain can influence brain function, yet its central neurobiological mechanisms in chronic low back pain (CLBP) remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate localized and long-range functional connectivity (FC) alterations in patients with mild to moderate CLBP using static/dynamic regional homogeneity (sReHo/dReHo) and seed-based FC, and to assess their statistical relationships with clinical pain and psychological metrics. title: Carotid atherosclerotic plaque characterization using dual-energy computed tomography angiography and its correlation with cerebral ischemic stroke.
summary: Carotid plaque vulnerability is a key risk factor for cerebral ischemic stroke (CIS). This study aimed to investigate the value of dual-energy computed tomography angiography (CTA) for carotid plaque diagnosis and its associated CIS occurrence. In this retrospective study, 103 patients underwent the initial dual-energy CTA for carotid plaque identification and the following brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for CIS detection. title: The impact of hearing loss on tinnitus-related brain reorganization: evidence from multimodal resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging.
summary: Whether hearing loss fundamentally alters tinnitus-related brain reorganization remains unclear. To address this issue, this study compared features from multimodal resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) between tinnitus patients with hearing loss (TIN + HL) and those without hearing loss (TIN - HL). A total of 38 patients with tinnitus (23 TIN + HL and 15 TIN - HL) and 28 healthy controls (HCs) underwent rs-fMRI. title: Structural alterations in the superior temporal gyrus associated with depressive symptoms in migraine without aura: a voxel-based morphometry and surface-based morphometry magnetic resonance imaging study.
summary: Migraine without aura (MwoA) frequently co-occurs with depressive symptoms, yet the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this comorbidity remain insufficiently characterized. This study integrated voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and surface-based morphometry (SBM) to compare gray matter volume (GMV) and cortical morphology between patients with MwoA and healthy controls (HC) and to further determine whether structural brain alterations vary across MwoA subgroups stratified by depressive symptom severity, thereby identifying potential structural correlates of depressive symptoms in this population. title: The DentoNeural Axis: A Piezo channel-mediated mechanosensory pathway linking tooth loss to cognitive decline.
summary: Two independent meta-analyses-one of 18 cohort studies (n = 356,297) and one dose-response analysis of 14 longitudinal studies (n = 34,074)-demonstrate dose-dependent associations between tooth loss and dementia. The latter reported hazard ratio (HR) 1.48 (95% CI 1.18-1.87) for cognitive impairment and HR 1.28 (95% CI 1.09-1.49) for dementia; the former reported relative risk (RR) 1.20 and 1.15 for the same outcomes. summary: Medical image classification faces multiple challenges, including heterogeneous lesion morphology, cross-modal representation discrepancy, and computational efficiency. title: Functional connectivity recovers canine-human network homology along the evolutionary cortical hierarchy.
summary: Mapping functional brain organization between species is a prerequisite for translating connectivity biomarkers from animal models to patients, but connectivity-based correspondence has been demonstrated almost exclusively in primates. We tested whether canine-human network homology can be recovered from functional connectivity alone, using only five network-level anatomical priors, and benchmarked a spectral manifold alignment framework (Laplacian-eigenmap embedding with Procrustes alignment on network centroids) against a simple connectivity-signature matching baseline. title: Pediatric Headache: A Practical Approach to Clinical Diagnosis and Management.
summary: Headache is among the most common neurological complaints of childhood and adolescence and can substantially impair school attendance and quality of life. A practical approach to the child with headache rests on four tasks: recognizing the primary headache phenotype, screening for the minority of children whose headache is secondary to another disorder, assessing how much the headache is disabling the child, and matching treatment intensity to that disability. title: How do Uncompensated Micro-Shifts Systematically Confound Low-Concentration Metabolite Quantification in 1H-MRS Analysis?
summary: Linear combination model fitting is widely used for spectral analysis in 1H-MRS but relies on basis sets with fixed spin-system parameters, implicitly neglecting the sensitivity of chemical shifts to physiological and pathological tissue microenvironments. This study systematically evaluated the impact of frequency perturbations on spectral analysis and reassessed the validity of the Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLB) as a quality-control metric for low-concentration metabolites. title: Evaluation of the brachial plexus and spinal cord with diffusion tensor imaging and synthetic MRI in obstetric brachial plexus palsy: DTI of brachial plexus and spinal cord in OBPP.
summary: Obstetric brachial plexus palsy (OBPP) is conventionally staged as a peripheral nerve injury, yet conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) poorly reflects microstructural neural and spinal cord changes. We evaluate whether magnetic resonance image compilation (MAGIC), a form of synthetic MRI, shows strong agreement with conventional T2-weighted short-tau inversion recovery (T2-STIR) for postganglionic injury detection, compare diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics between injured and adjacent intact segments of the brachial plexus and spinal cord, and explore whether these metrics predict recovery at 2-year follow-up in infants with OBPP. title: In Vivo Dynamic D2O-MRI for Quantifying Apparent CSF Water Renewal Across Ventricular and Extraventricular Compartments.
summary: The choroid plexus has long been regarded as the principal source of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), yet this view remains unresolved. We developed a dynamic indirect D2O MRI approach to quantify regional apparent CSF water renewal in vivo in rats at 9.4 T. Rats were scanned at 9.4 T using spin-echo echo-planar imaging during intravenous D2O infusion (10.69-s temporal resolution, 150 × 150 μm2 in-plane resolution). title: Effects of morning versus evening high-intensity exercise on electroencephalographic and autonomic responses in middle-aged women.
summary: The time of day at which exercise is performed influences physiological responses and performance, and thus its health benefits. This study investigated whether electroencephalographic (EEG) and autonomic nervous system responses to morning versus evening exercise differed in middle-aged women. Thirty women aged 50-60 years were randomly assigned to a morning or evening exercise group. Participants were asked to sleep for seven to eight hours before testing. title: Neurotologic and MRI Correlates of Idiopathic Acute Unilateral Audiovestibulopathy.
summary: Although MRI can aid in detecting idiopathic acute unilateral audiovestibulopathy (iAUAV), the relationship between imaging and neurotologic findings remains unclear. We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of patients diagnosed with iAUAV at a tertiary hospital in South Korea between March 2018 and September 2025. Neurotologic and imaging data on heavily T2-weighted 3D fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences were included for analysis. Eighty-four patients with iAUAV were included in the analysis. title: The weight of junk food: Smaller hippocampal, amygdala, and prefrontal volumes in adolescents-The Cogni-Action Project.
source: PubMed · Appl Psychol Health Well Being
summary: Most studies investigating diet-brain relationships in youth focus on single foods. Whether the joint consumption of multiple food groups is associated with neuroanatomy during adolescence remains largely unexplored, particularly outside high-income countries. In this cross-sectional study, 61 Chilean adolescents (11.6 ± 1.07 years; 42.6% girls) underwent T1-weighted MRI. title: Information avant la lettre: The mathematical constitution of brain waves in early EEG analysis (1929-1932).
summary: This article examines the epistemological conditions under which the brain's electrophysiological trace was first constituted as a mathematical object of analysis. Rather than treating information as a cultural metaphor externally projected onto the brain, the paper reconstructs how specific tools of signal analysis made the trace into an object that the informational lineage would come to require. Hans Berger's research of 1929-1931 secured the trace as an effect of nervous processes in the brain, but read it as the signal of a single source. title: Early postnatal brain volumes and two-year cognitive outcomes in preterm infants: An exploratory machine learning study.
summary: Premature birth is associated with an increased risk of cognitive and motor developmental problems. Early prediction of these outcomes is crucial for timely intervention and adequate follow-up. This study aimed to predict cognitive and motor outcomes in preterm-born infants using brain volumetric features in combination with clinical and demographic perinatal characteristics, and to compare the performance of three different machine learning algorithms. title: Inflections in adolescent cortical maturation signal psychopathology risk
summary: Cerebral cortical maturation supports emotional, social, and cognitive development during adolescence1. Neurodevelopmental theories of psychiatric illnesses, which peak in onset around age 182, implicate subtle alterations in adolescent cortical development3. title: Neural Dissociation of Cognitive Maps and Graphs in the Human Brain
summary: Cognitive maps and graphs offer two distinct ways of organizing knowledge: maps arrange items within a spatial layout, whereas graphs thread them together through experiential transitions. However, spatial proximity and experiential contiguity are typically correlated, and content represented in one format can often be transformed into the other, making their neural representations difficult to disentangle. title: A touch that lingers: synchronized patting strengthens neural tracking of auditory rhythm in newborns
summary: Rhythmic auditory stimulation in early life rarely occurs in isolation. Caregivers naturally combine singing and speech with rhythmic touch, rocking, and visual cues. Newborns are sensitive to auditory rhythm from birth, yet little is known about how temporally aligned information across sensory modalities shapes the neural encoding of auditory rhythmic structure. Here, we tested whether rhythmic touch can alter how the newborn brain tracks an ongoing auditory signal beyond the period of tactile stimulation. title: Modulation of the speed of Intrinsic Alpha Frequency (IAF) with tACS modulates variability of illusory speech perception
summary: Navigating the world requires our brains to constantly process a massive influx of information from the environment. One of the most remarkable yet complex feats the human brain performs daily is speech perception. It is a multifaceted, hierarchical process that relies heavily on the integration of auditory and visual cues, particularly in noisy environments. Neural integration of these streams is hypothesized to depend on temporal mechanisms governed by individual alpha frequency (IAF, 8-12 Hz), which serves as a key neural correlate of the temporal binding window (TBW). title: Nimbus Studio reproduces reference BCI decoding pipelines: a validation study on public benchmarks across protocols and paradigms
summary: Nimbus Studio is a visual pipeline platform for brain-computer interface (BCI) experiments: researchers assemble preprocessing, feature extraction, decoding, and evaluation over public benchmark datasets or their own recordings, with cross-validated evaluation protocols (including leave-one-subject-out), BIDS export, and bring-your-own Python model classes. title: EEG Entrainment to Non-Speech Rhythmic Patterns Associated with Dimensions of Language Performance
summary: Developmental dyslexia (DLX) affects 5-12% of the global population and impairs learning to read. Entrainment, the coupling of brain oscillations to speech rhythms, is essential for encoding phonological representations. We investigated whether brain entrainment to non-speech rhythms could predict DLX in 48 participants listening to white noise amplitude-modulated at rates matching Spanish speech units.
